correctness.rationale:
The defining bracket forces every automorphism to satisfy \(\phi(e_1)=\beta e_1\), \(\phi(e_2)=e_2+b\), and \(\phi|_Z=B\). For \(x=u e_1+c e_2+v\), the action is \((u,c,v)\mapsto(\beta u,c,cv+Bv)\). Thus \(c=\chi(x)\) is invariant; for \(c
e0\), translation kills \(v\) and scaling separates \(u=0\) from \(u
e0\), while for \(c=0\) the independent scalar and general-linear actions give exactly four zero-fiber strata when \(n\ge3\). The finite-field orbit sizes follow by direct counting and are independently replayed by the packaged checker.

value.rationale: The source identifies \(L_n\) as the universal non-nilpotent non-Lie one-derived Leibniz algebra in characteristic different from \(2\), so its internal symmetry orbits are a natural structural invariant of the classified family. The orbit theorem gives a basis-free stratification by the adjoint scalar, square map, derived line, and center, and the finite-field consequence is unexpectedly dimension-stable: every dimension \(n\ge3\) has exactly \(2q+2\) element orbits. This is more than a raw group-order calculation and supplies a reusable normal form for element-level questions in the entire family.
